pr_title: Add back editor support for non-standard time signatures
pr_body:
Closes #16419.

First of all, note the "add *back*" part, because this pull aims to bring feature parity with stable first and foremost. I know arbitrary `n/m` time signatures are wanted, but that requires figuring out a new file format for beatmaps which I don't want to get into right now.

This is how the time signature control looks now:

![osu_2022-01-22_21-01-33](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/20418176/150657957-30c5232d-2879-4627-a06d-97cd8e493947.jpg)

Other caveats:

* Code-wise, 735414bc is the large part of this diff in terms of files touched, and may be controversial. I found using the `TimeSignatures` enum turbo sketchy for this feature in general. The fact that you can cast a number to any enumeration type and get back a valid value even if the numerical value isn't defined on the enum to me was always a *downside* of C# enums, and so continuing to use that quirk for this just felt wrong and awkward and cast-heavy. So I substituted in a proper type for this case; it also paves the way for when someone one day does decide to add arbitrary denominator support.

  Can revert if there's disagreement, though.
* UI-wise I decided to not follow stable, which had both a set of radio buttons for 3/4 and 4/4, as well as a "custom" radio button with a spinner attached. To simplify I just kept the textbox. I think that's simpler and better in general.
* Note that taiko and mania bar lines will not regenerate if you change a timing point inside editor, until editor is exited and re-entered. That's a pre-existing issue that needs to be addressed separately (bar line hit objects need to be regenerated on any timing point changes).

issue_context.title: Add support for nonstandard time signatures
issue_context.body:
Splitting from https://github.com/ppy/osu/issues/12020.

The goal is to support custom time signatures like stable did:

![](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/80785742/111513293-8f822c00-8748-11eb-84aa-3c0c65e95480.png)

Moreover, currently when a map with a custom timing signature is opened, clicking on a row on the timing screen that has a custom signature crashes with

```
[runtime] 2022-01-11 21:22:40 [error]: System.ArgumentNullException: Value cannot be null. (Parameter 'element')
```

comments: For reference, there is already an issue thread open tracking the addition of nonstandard time signatures (https://github.com/ppy/osu/issues/2316).
And a PR which is stuck in limbo https://github.com/ppy/osu/pull/2403
That issue and that PR are talking about beat divisors and not the meter of the song though, aren't they? Like the beat snap and the timing signature on the timing point aren't the same thing?

Right. Considering this causes a crash it'd be best to get things working again as a starting point. Keep in mind that going forward, people are going to ask for changing the denominator as well. But that adds quite a bit of complexity (and requires new storage in the beatmap format) so would be a follow-up effort.

review_comments: Looks to be missing handling for custom numerators. On checking with osu!stable it does work differently for custom numerators, but I'm not sure what the algorithm behind it is. Can be left for a follow-up if complicated though.
Purposefully not added to not scope creep (and because I'm not sure how nightcore should even work for odd time signatures like 7/4, for instance).
I see, might as well have mentioned that in OP. Sounds fair.
Just to note it here, osu!(stable) seems to have the nominator lower limit set to 5 for the "custom" time signature option, but I suppose there is no issue with supporting 2/4 (and 1/4 as well? 🤔)
I've actually been linked maps which were mapped in 2/4. 1/4 I'm not super sure about, can disallow.
I think it's fine to allow.
I think it is more suitable for this to be a `readonly struct` instead given that it only holds immutable primitive values shared across components.

I purposefully did not use readonly struct. You would be able to then do `new TimeSignature()` which would be zero initialised and therefore invalid. And you can neither disallow that or add default values to a readonly struct.
The point about invalidly zero initialised and also not have default values sounds fair. You might as well make `SimpleTriple` and `SimpleQuadruple` statics initialised once rather than per access.
